ai.description: *Microhyla eos* is a tiny frog (16–18 mm) with a reddish-brown dorsum and a dark lateral band. It features a distinct, pale mid-dorsal stripe and lacks webbing on the toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla eos* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright orange-red patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: The Arunachal Chorus Frog inhabits subtropical broadleaf forests and marshy wetlands within the Himalayan foothills, typically at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Arunachal Chorus Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging during the monsoon to congregate in large, vocalizing groups near temporary rain pools to breed.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla eos* breeds in seasonal pools during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of eggs that hatch into free-swimming, exotrophic larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Microhyla eos* is endemic to the Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh, India, occurring at elevations between 400 and 600 meters within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The Arunachal Chorus Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of rapid, repetitive pulses, typically heard emanating from flooded forest floors.
